evidence.finding: The public release provides darwin, linux and windows archives for amd64 and arm64. The application is a terminal UI using tmux and git, not a standalone graphical desktop app.

evidence.title: Claude Squad v1.0.20 source
evidence.locator: Go source in app, cmd, config, session and ui; web app boilerplate
evidence.finding: The executable is a local Bubble Tea terminal UI that creates and attaches tmux sessions, sends prompts and renders diffs. The repository has no product web-session interface, native phone app, human account/member system, SSO integration or telemetry configuration. The web directory is website boilerplate, not a released session client.

evidence.title: Claude Squad v1.0.20 source
evidence.locator: InstanceData; SaveInstances; session/instance.go; app event handlers
evidence.finding: Persistent InstanceData stores session title, path, branch, status, program, worktree and diff state. Human UI actions create sessions. There is no separate issue/task store, product coordinator role/delegation tool, schedule/webhook starter or team user input transport. AutoYes acknowledges prompts in an existing session rather than starting a new task.

evidence.title: Claude Squad v1.0.20 source
evidence.locator: TmuxSession.Start; session/git/worktree*.go; config and command launcher
evidence.finding: The app runs tmux new-session on its current host with a Git worktree as cwd. Built-in execution has no vendor compute provisioner, container runtime or VM launcher. Tmux detachment preserves processes only while that execution host stays running.

evidence.title: Claude Squad v1.0.20 source
evidence.finding: PushChanges commits, pushes/syncs the branch with git/gh repo sync and optionally opens gh browse --branch. Bounded inspection of the Git/session action code found no PR create/update/review/merge management call.
